text:
sara: Heads up — Support escalated a customer in eu-west: p95 jumped ~2.3x since yesterday's runtime roll (version 2.8.1). Ticket #4282 attached.

support-bot: Customer sample: 2026-03-16T09:12Z, route=/v1/generate, 95th=420ms -> 980ms, p99=1.8s. No errors, just slow.

jamie: Thanks — is this isolated to that tenant or cohorted? Any recent config overrides?

sara: Appears only for traffic pinned to eu-west-1b (cohort size ~12k req/day). No config overrides from the customer. They use a long-context workload (seq len ~2k).

ben: Noted. Post-roll we changed late-binding kernel selector to prefer the new quant scheduler on all hosts. Could be a scheduler interaction with long sequences.

lucy: Quick checks: 1) are KV cache hit rates degraded for that tenant? 2) any auth token refresh storms? 3) per-host CPU/GPU utilization for 1b cluster?

mike: KV cache hit rates look normal in metrics dashboard for eu-west-1b. Auth refreshes spike earlier but correlate to a different tenant. GPU util on hosts with high latencies is ~95% and queue depth increased.

jamie: If queue depth up + GPU saturation on some hosts, requests may be getting queued on slow nodes -> sticky latency. Any routing affinity changes in the rollout?

ben: We did flip the routing optimizer to prefer fewer cross-AZ handoffs for affinity (reduce cross AZ p50). That could cause load concentration if shard mapping changed.

sara: Support requested repro steps. I'm dropping what I used below. Please try locally against staging with an EU-like cohort.

sara: Repro steps:
```
# sample single-request test hitting eu-west routes
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Region: eu-west" \ 
  -d '{"input":"<2k tokens of repeated prompt>", "max_tokens":512}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Expect: p95 ~400ms in staging baseline. If you see >700ms, we hit the same regression.

lucy: I ran 50 serial requests against a staging pool with quant scheduler enabled. Observed p95=820ms when traffic pinned to the same host shard; distributed requests p95 ~410ms. So affinity -> saturation looks likely.

ben: Hypothesis: routing affinity + kernel scheduler change moved long-sequence heavy shard onto fewer GPUs; scheduler picks suboptimal kernels for long sequences under 95% util.

jamie: Mitigations:
- immediate: enable per-route fallback to pre-roll kernel selector for that cohort (fast config flip).
- short-term: enable traffic-shed for the affected tenant to reduce request rate until we patch.
- medium: revert routing-affinity change for eu-west or increase shard spreading.
- long-term: tune scheduler heuristics for sequence length distribution and add soft caps on per-host concurrency.

mike: I'll push a config: `route_override: { region: eu-west, kernel_selector: prefer-old }` to canary 10% now and monitor.

ops-bot: Deploy initiated: route override to 10% canary (eu-west) by mike at 2026-03-16T09:32Z.

lucy: After canary flip p95 for that cohort dropped from 980ms -> 430ms in 30m sampling. Good signal.

ben: OK. Plan: roll the override to 100% for eu-west, open a postmortem to track scheduler change + routing affinity. We'll also add synthetic workload tests for long contexts to our CI perf suite.

sara: I'll update the support ticket and give the customer the mitigation steps + ETA for permanent fix. Thanks team :heart: 

jamie: One follow-up: add a brief note in release notes about the scheduler heuristic change and recommend a staged rollout for high-seq-length customers.

sara: Will do. Closing loop when rollback fully propagated.
